mike_support: Hey team — customer suzy_customer reporting intermittent streaming cutoffs for SSE. They see full messages sometimes but often partial output then no reconnect. Happens on Safari and Chrome behind Akamai. CustomerID: C-8291, request id: r_0a9b3c. Repro steps attached below.

suzy_customer: Adding repro: open the app, trigger long streaming completion (~45s tokens). After ~12-18s stream stalls with 'eventsource onerror' and never reconnects. If I refresh page later I see the remaining tokens in logs, so server finished but client didn't get them.

mike_support: Repro steps pasted from the customer's page:
1) page loads https://app.example.com/chat
2) browser creates EventSource to /v1/streams/chat?r=requestid
3) onmessage starts, partial data arrives then stops
4) network tab shows 200 then connection goes to 0 bytes for a long time; sometimes an HTTP 304 shows up from Akamai for the final chunks

alex_eng: Can you paste headers from a failing request? I want to check caching and connection headers.

suzy_customer: Here is a copy from the devtools Network > Response Headers (trimmed):

"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\nContent-Type: text/event-stream\nCache-Control: public, max-age=3600\nETag: \"abc123\"\nConnection: keep-alive\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\nAccess-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.example.com\nAccess-Control-Allow-Credentials: true\n\n"

sophia_devex: Uh — Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600 on an SSE endpoint is a red flag. CDNs will happily cache or serve 304s for requests if they think the origin hasn't changed. SSE must be uncacheable and should include no-transform for many CDNs. Also ETag + 304 behavior can break streaming clients which expect a live body.

alex_eng: Confirming. If Akamai returns 304 for the streamed connection it effectively terminates the body for the client. Also some Akamai edge rules will convert responses to a cached object and then close TCP while the origin continues to send. That's why logs show server completed but client didn't.

infra-bot: deploy-notification: Edge header injection experiment rolled to staging earlier (edge-headers-2026-02-10). Possibly related.

mike_support: Customer said this started ~24h after a platform config change. Could be that header injection experiment. Any quick mitigations we can ask them to try?

alex_eng: Immediate mitigation for customer-side: use polyfill that uses XMLHttpRequest streaming fallback (eventsource-polyfill) — but beware CORS preflight caching. Better server-side fix: ensure SSE endpoints set "Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate" and remove ETag for streaming endpoints. Also add "Cache-Control: no-transform" and set "Surrogate-Control: no-store" for Akamai.

sophia_devex: Example header set we should recommend to customers and to push from edge:

```
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate, no-transform
Pragma: no-cache
Surrogate-Control: no-store
Connection: keep-alive
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.example.com
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
```

mike_support: I tried curl --no-buffer against origin, stream arrives fine; with Akamai in front I can reproduce the 304 behavior. Example:

curl -i -N "https://edge.example.com/v1/streams/chat?r=r_0a9b3c" -H "Origin: https://app.example.com" --no-buffer

When routed to origin: continuous chunked body.
When routed via Akamai: headers include ETag and Cache-Control public leading to 304 responses mid-stream.

alex_eng: Action items: 1) Roll back/disable edge header injection for SSE paths edge rule (edge-headers-2026-02-10) 2) Add explicit SSE-safe headers on origin for /v1/streams/* 3) Add filter in CDN config to never cache content-type text/event-stream and never generate 304 for streaming connections.

sophia_devex: Note about Safari: Safari can aggressively buffer HTTP/2 responses at proxies; we should also suggest customers use direct websocket or fall back to long-poll if behind aggressive proxies. But primary fix is to stop CDN caching of SSE.

suzy_customer: Would appreciate a small patch we can test quickly — we can flip a feature flag on our end to point to a staging domain if you give us one.

alex_eng: I'll create a staging edge rule right now and post a test URL. Also we'll push the header rollback to canary and monitor. Mike, can you send suzy the staging URL once ready?

mike_support: Will do. Also documenting troubleshooting notes for support KB: 1) Check Response Headers for Cache-Control / ETag on SSE endpoints 2) Reproduce by bypassing CDN (curl --no-buffer) 3) If CDN shows 304/304-like behavior, escalate to infra to set surrogate rules 4) Suggest temporary client fallback: polyfill XHR streaming but disable caching on preflight responses.

sophia_devex: Quick code snippet for a resilient client fallback (use only as last resort):

```
// tiny XHR streaming fallback
function xhrStream(url, onChunk) {
  var xhr = new XMLHttpRequest();
  xhr.open('GET', url, true);
  xhr.withCredentials = true;
  xhr.onreadystatechange = function() {
    if (xhr.readyState === 3) {
      var chunk = xhr.responseText.substring(lastIndex);
      lastIndex = xhr.responseText.length;
      onChunk(chunk);
    }
  };
  xhr.send(null);
}
```

alex_eng: I'm going to file INFRA-4218 to disable the header injection on SSE paths and add the CDN rule to exclude text/event-stream from caching. I'll post updates here.

infra-bot: ticket INFRA-4218 created by alex_eng: Disable edge header injection for SSE and add surrogate no-cache rule.

mike_support: Thanks all — I'll keep suzy updated and follow up once INFRA-4218 lands. If anyone hits similar customer reports, point them to this thread.
